metadata.note: The Detroit and Charlevoix Railroad, Frederic (junction with the Michigan Central Mackinaw Division, Crawford County) - Deward - Blue Lake Junction - Lake Harold - Alba (GR&I crossing) - Jordan River - Marble/Wards (East Jordan & Southern crossing) - East Jordan (South Arm), Mich., 42.4 mi. Two features share identical geometry under Rule 4's ownership split: the D&C ran it 1901 - 31 Oct 1916, the Michigan Central from 1 Nov 1916 as its East Jordan Branch.
geometry_sources: Frederic - East Jordan: OpenHistoricalMap ways 198929360 and 198929363 (USGS Topo / 3DEP-derived), geometry only; OHM dates not used. OpenStreetMap carries nothing for this road.
not_yet_sourced: mc-east-jordan-branch: the PASSENGER END YEAR is [OPEN]. The segment ends at 1921, the last year with explicit passenger evidence (Charlevoix County Herald, 12 Aug 1921); the true end lies between 1921 and c.1932. The 25 Sep 1925 employee-timetable train (Nos. 97/98, tri-weekly) would move the confirmed end to 1925 if shown to be a mixed carrying passengers. Leads: ICC decisions 170 ICC 775 (FD 8545, 1930) and 187 ICC 339 (FD 9230, 1932) on HathiTrust; Charlevoix County Herald 1922-1932 (not on Chronicling America - every probe 404'd); Official Guide 1926/1930; Michigan PUC annual reports. If the two abandonments ended passenger trains in different years, split the feature at Marble.

Operator-change conflict: Wikipedia gives a corporate merger into the Michigan Central on 27 Sep 1912 (renamed East Jordan Branch), but the contemporaneous MC circular (Charlevoix County Herald 3 Nov 1916; DFP-1916-1103) says the MC took over operation and renamed it only from 1 Nov 1916. The map splits at 1916 (who ran the trains); Moody's 1918 or the MC 1916 annual report would settle the corporate date. The MC's 1 May 1907 stock purchase did not change the operator and is not a split; RG-1905-0818's 'MC absorbs the D&C' is premature.

Blue Lake Branch (Blue Lake Junction MP 14.4 west ~8 mi to Crooked Lake, Squaw Lake, Blue Lake): NOT DRAWN. Fowler stars its stations as 'shown in 1905G, was a passenger service operated?' - doubting it himself - while the Michigan Railroad Commission's 21 Oct 1909 inspection says the D&C's branches to forest terminals are 'used exclusively for logging purposes'. No confirmed passenger year; conflict recorded, not resolved.
Sundays: no source says whether the D&C ran on Sundays 1901-1916; the 1918 MC card is daily except Sunday.
Incorporation date 1 Jan (Wikipedia) vs 2 Jan (MCR-1902) vs articles reported filed 4 Jan 1901 (GRP); immaterial to the drawn years.
metadata.omitted: Not drawn (Rule 1): David Ward's private Frederic & Charlevoix logging road c.1893/1896-1900 (no public trains; 'has been a logging road, but now ... will be fully operated with passenger trains', PHTH-1901-0819); the Blue Lake Branch and ~40 mi of logging branches and spurs (MRC 1909: 'used exclusively for logging purposes'); any MC freight between the unknown last passenger train and the 1931/1932-33 abandonments. Never built: East Jordan - Charlevoix extension (c.13 mi) and the MC's 1907 Deward - Grayling cut-off.
metadata.rule4_note: Michigan Central colour pulled programmatically from the 'Michigan Central Railroad' features of michigan_central_detroit_chicago.geojson. Known pre-existing Rule 4 mismatch NOT fixed here: michigan_central_michigan_network.geojson's seven features carry their own colours under combined 'Predecessor / Michigan Central Railroad' company strings, each spanning the predecessor and MC eras unsplit.

properties.line: Detroit and Charlevoix: Frederic – East Jordan
properties.speed_source: estimated: derived from the report's quoted schedules - 1906 eastbound 42.4 mi in 3 h 25 min (~20 km/h), 1902 westbound ~2 h 15 min (~30 km/h); mixed train. Rounded, not a published average (Rule 3).
properties.geometry_source: OpenHistoricalMap (overpass-api.openhistoricalmap.org), traced with opstrace.py. The whole line is OHM way 198929360 (name 'East Jordan Branch', operator 'Detroit and Charlevoix Railroad'; Frederic junction - Blue Lake Junction, 14.7 mi) and OHM way 198929363 (name 'Detroit and Charlevoix Railroad'; Blue Lake Junction - East Jordan and on), both source USGS Topo / USGS 3DEP. OHM's start_date/end_date on these ways (1893-1932/1933) were NOT used for any year on this map - only the geometry. OpenStreetMap was probed first: no way in the region carries old_railway_operator (or abandoned:railway) for the D&C under any spelling tried (D&C, Detroit and Charlevoix, Detroit & Charlevoix, Michigan Central, MC, MCRR, NYC, New York Central) - fetch_operator_ways returned 0 ways - and OSM's untagged railway=abandoned ways and rail-trails in the corridor were folded into the router but none was used. Waypoints are pinned to real vertices of the OHM line (Frederic junction, two vertices on the loop north of Deward, Deward, Blue Lake Junction, the crossing with OHM's East Jordan & Southern way 198929369 at Marble/Wards, and East Jordan) plus the Nominatim village of Alba (0.4 km off the line). Nominatim's Deward (hamlet) pulled the router onto a 0.6 mi untagged OHM logging spur, so it was replaced by the nearest D&C vertex; Wards, Blue Lake, Jordan River and Lake Harold geocoded to wrong places or to water and were not used; Marble returned nothing. Simplified Douglas-Peucker 8 m, then trim_reversals.
properties.geometry_quality: Frederic - East Jordan: drawn 42.3 mi against a documented 42.4 mi (MRR-TT1 mileposts, East Jordan MP 42.4; Fowler 42.5; Wikipedia 42.66; ICC dockets 6.5 + 36.31 = 42.81). 100% of the router's mileage is on OHM ways named for the D&C (42.3 mi before simplification); NO straight-line or approximated leg. Milepost check against MRR-TT1: Blue Lake Jct MP 14.4 vs 14.7 traced; Alba MP 24.5 vs 24.6; Marble/Wards (East Jordan & Southern crossing) MP 36.1 vs 36.4; East Jordan MP 42.4 vs 42.3 - so the long loop north of Deward (the line runs ~8 mi north from Frederic and doubles back south to Deward at MP 11.9, where the direct chord is only ~6 mi) is the documented route, not a router detour. Frederic end: the OHM line meets the Michigan Central Mackinaw Division ~175 m from OSM's live track, ~0.3 km south of the village centre. East Jordan end: cut at the OHM vertex on the west side of the South Arm nearest MP 42.4; OHM's way runs a further 2.1 mi north up the west shore, beyond any documented station, and that tail is not drawn. Alignment era: OHM's trace is from USGS topographic mapping of the abandoned grade, i.e. the line as last built; no realignment of the main line between 1901 and abandonment is recorded in the report, so the same geometry serves both the D&C (1901-1916) and Michigan Central (1916-1921) eras. Geometry is shared identically by both features (Rule 4 ownership split).

segments.note: Detroit and Charlevoix Railroad, incorporated by the David Ward estate in January 1901 (1, 2 or 4 Jan - sources differ) on the grade of Ward's private Frederic & Charlevoix logging road. Public service began September 1901: operation Frederic - Alba reported 6 Sep 1901 (LSJ-1901-0906), the first train East Jordan - Frederic ran 11 Sep 1901 (GRP-1901-0911), and the line was completed to South Arm (East Jordan) 16 Sep 1901 (MCR-1903). One mixed train each way daily carried the passengers throughout: MCR-1902 '1 mixed train each way daily between Frederic and South Arm'; a March 1902 card lv South Arm 9:00 am, lv Frederic 4:00 pm; briefly two round trips in summer 1904 (CCH-1904-0903); one round trip in 1906 (CCH-1906-0217) and 1907 (MCR-1907); 'the public is handled by a mixed train service' (Michigan Railroad Commission inspection, 21 Oct 1909); D&C fare 3c/mile until the takeover (CCH 3 Nov 1916). Interchange with the Michigan Central at Frederic; used the GR&I depot at Alba. The Michigan Central bought all the D&C stock on 1 May 1907 but the D&C kept operating under its own name, offices and fares; the MC took over operation on 1 Nov 1916 (MC circular, CCH 3 Nov 1916), so this feature ends at 1916 and the Michigan Central: East Jordan Branch feature continues it. Wikipedia's 27 Sep 1912 merger date conflicts with the 1916 circular - see layer metadata. Ward's pre-1901 logging road, the Blue Lake Branch and the ~40 mi of logging spurs carried no confirmed passengers and are not drawn (Rule 1). Headway 1440 min = one round trip a day, an estimate from the quoted schedules; whether Sundays ran before 1918 is not stated.
sources: Segment-level: start (Sept 1901) from GRP-1901-0911, LSJ-1901-0906 and MCR-1903 as quoted by michiganrailroads.com; mixed-train passenger service 1902-1909 from MCR-1902, CCH-1906-0217, MCR-1907 and the 1909 Michigan Railroad Commission inspection; end of D&C operation 31 Oct 1916 from the Charlevoix County Herald, 3 Nov 1916. Headway is an estimate from those schedules.

segments.note: Michigan Central (New York Central System) East Jordan Branch, the former Detroit and Charlevoix, operated by the MC from 1 Nov 1916: an MC circular said the D&C 'running between Frederic and East Jordan, will be taken over by the Michigan Central and thereafter will be known as the East Jordan branch', fare cut to 2c/mile (CCH 3 Nov 1916). An MC timetable of 30 Jun 1918 shows one round trip daily except Sunday (No. 1 lv East Jordan 8:00 am ar Frederic 10:45; return lv Frederic 2:15 pm ar East Jordan 4:45 pm); a new fall schedule from 26 Oct 1919 (CCH 24 Oct 1919); and a card effective 10 Aug 1921 ran No. 1 Grayling 6:00 am - Frederic 6:30 - East Jordan 9:00 am and No. 2 out of East Jordan at 11:00 am with a 'close connection for Detroit' (CCH 12 Aug 1921) - the last explicit passenger evidence found. END YEAR IS [OPEN]: passenger service is confirmed to 1921 only. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. A tri-weekly scheduled train (Nos. 97/98, Tue/Thu/Sat) appears in MC Employee Timetable #405 of 25 Sep 1925, very probably the mixed but not shown to carry passengers; Marble - East Jordan (6.5 mi) was approved for abandonment by ICC FD 8545 (30 Oct 1930) and the Michigan PUC (1931), and Frederic - Marble (36.31 mi) by ICC FD 9230 (7 Mar 1932). None of those is a passenger end date. The true end lies between 1921 and c.1932. Do not extend without evidence. Headway 1440 min = one round trip a day (except Sunday 1918-1921), an estimate from the quoted cards. The 1921 trains ran through to Grayling over the MC Mackinaw Division, which is drawn separately.
sources: Segment-level: start (MC operation from 1 Nov 1916) from the Charlevoix County Herald, 3 Nov 1916; 1918 service from the MC timetable of 30 Jun 1918 as quoted by michiganrailroads.com; 1919 and 1921 service from the Charlevoix County Herald, 24 Oct 1919 and 12 Aug 1921. The end year is NOT SOURCED - 1921 is the last confirmed year, not an ending. Abandonment dockets (not passenger end dates) per abandonedrails.com.
